description: Indiana 211 connects residents with local health and human service resources. Use it to locate providers for food, housing, utilities and other needs.
introduction: Indiana 211 connects residents with local health and human service resources. Use it to locate providers for food, housing, utilities and other needs.

sections.who: You can request referrals without first qualifying for a particular benefit. The organization receiving the referral applies its own eligibility and intake rules.
sections.get: A navigator helps identify relevant community providers. FSSA also links to a ZIP-based resource search and Community Compass food resources.
sections.docs: Prepare your city or ZIP code, the help needed and any deadline. For a referral conversation, describe the issue before sending financial or identity records.
sections.apply:
1. Contact the service

    Call 211 or 866-211-9966, or text your ZIP code to 898-211.

  2. Explain your situation

    Mention immediate problems and ask which organizations serve your address.

  3. Save referral details

    Record the contact, intake requirements and opening hours, then contact the provider directly.
sections.after: If the first provider cannot help, return to 211 for alternatives. Check operating hours on the current service website before calling.
sections.sources: Reviewed October 1, 2026 using FSSA Indiana 211 contacts and search tools, Indiana 211 service information. The administering provider determines eligibility and availability.

faqs: Does 211 approve SNAP or pay a bill?
No. It helps connect you to the relevant provider.
Yes. FSSA links to a resource search by ZIP code.
Can I ask about several needs?
Explain the needs together so the navigator can identify relevant services.
What if a referral is unavailable?
Tell 211 what happened and ask about another provider.

provenance.review_scope: Published eligibility and intake facts; no inferred payment guarantees.
